passages.provision_quote: the single-member districts for Congress reflected in Assembly Bill 604 of the 2025–26 Regular Session pursuant to the requirements of Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 21400) of Division 21 of the Elections Code shall temporarily be used for every congressional election for a term of office commencing on or after the date this subdivision becomes operative and before the certification of new congressional boundary lines drawn by the Citizens Redistricting Commission pursuant to subdivision (d).
passages.note: ACA 8 temporarily substitutes legislature-drawn (AB 604) maps for the Commission's, with court jurisdiction over challenges, while the same measure restores Commission authority in 2031 and declares state policy support for independent, nonpartisan commissions, so it shows direction but not one clean chair.

rows.reasoning: As author of ACA 8, Rivas backs a one-cycle, 'notwithstanding the authority of the Citizens Redistricting Commission' substitution of legislature-drawn congressional maps (AB 604) with California Supreme Court jurisdiction over challenges, framed as an 'Election Rigging Response' to Texas. But the same measure declares it 'the policy of the State of California to support the use of fair, independent, and nonpartisan redistricting commissions nationwide' and has the Commission 'continue to adjust the boundary lines' from 2031 onward, so it does not establish a standing choice among 'independent citizens' commissions with no elected officials involved at any level', 'independent redistricting commissions with equal representation from both major parties', or 'state legislatures with court oversight to prevent extreme partisan bias' — it shows only that he will deviate from the commission to counter a perceived partisan threat, not which rung he holds generally.
